lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Building a Fueling Meal
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: serving and storage

objective: Given a finished no-heat food item, learners independently decide the correct serving portion and storage method (refrigerate, cover, label) without adult step-by-step direction, and justify both decisions.
scenario: Without being told the steps, the learner is given a finished (or previously assembled) no-heat food item and must decide, on their own, how much to serve now and how to properly store the rest.
safetyNotes: No heat source or sharp tool is needed for serving or storage decisions in this lesson.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real finished food item isn't available to serve and store, the learner instead is given a written description of a finished food item and explains, in writing, the serving portion and storage decision they would make and why.

tasks.directions: Quickly recall: name one food you already know needs to be refrigerated after serving, and one that doesn't.
Serve an appropriate portion of your food item and store the rest correctly (covered, labeled if needed, and refrigerated if the food requires it).

prompts.text: Describe your serving portion and your storage method, and explain why you chose that storage method for this specific food.
Stored food is covered or sealed, not left open.
Stored food is in the correct location for its type (refrigerator vs. counter-safe).

tasks.directions: Rate your serving-and-storage confidence and select a next step.

prompts.text: Rate your confidence in making serving and storage decisions on your own (very / somewhat / not yet), cite the specific decision you made today as evidence, and choose: ready to try a trickier food item, ready to review this again, or need a different explanation.

remediation: If the learner stores a perishable item at room temperature, reteach by sorting five example foods into 'needs the fridge' and 'doesn't' before returning to the real storage decision.
extension: Repeat the task with a food item that has a less obvious storage answer (like a cut fruit or a dairy-based item) and explain the reasoning that made it trickier.
